messages:
Morgan: Heads-up — noticed a new spike in host-side CPU while profiling streaming requests to the 4G family. p95 decode latency up ~18% since yesterday's deploy. attaching a short flame and a few traces.
Sasha: ugh. is this the tokenization path or something in the ingress framing?
Morgan: looks like a mix. flame shows heavy time in proto unpack + header parsing + writev syscall churn. KV-cache hits look stable. KV thrash not the culprit here.
Raj: any evidence it’s gRPC/HTTP2 overhead? HPACK or frame processing can bite when we stream small chunks.
Morgan: exact stack samples: `proto.unmarshalHeader -> http2.readFrame -> grpc.(*serverStream).SendMsg -> syscall.writev` — lots of tiny writev calls.
Ben: how tiny? we saw earlier that writev <512B kills throughput for high qps streams.
Morgan: here's a quick aggregate from the pprof probe (one minute window):
```
writev_calls: 14.6k/s
avg_write_bytes: 420
syscall_latency_p95: 1.2ms
grpc_send_batch_count: 3.8k/s
```
Sasha: that avg_write_bytes is the smoking gun. lots of small frames. are we sending token-by-token from host-side tokenizer?
Morgan: yes — host tokenizer currently flushes each chunk to the stream as it finishes. combined with our current batching heuristic (max_batch_delay=5ms, min_batch_tokens=1) it prefers latency -> lots of microwrites.
perf-bot: CI trace label: `ingress/streaming/writev-churn` — regression introduced in rev r14532 (deploy 3309994000).
Raj: r14532 was the kernel-selection tweak + change to continuous-push behavior in the tokenizer worker. probably introduced a change to flush semantics.
Ben: quick mitigation ideas: 1) coalesce writes on host before calling SendMsg (socket buffer + writev), 2) change tokenizer to aggregate N tokens or bytes before flush, 3) adjust batching heuristic to favor small coalescing window when qps high.
Sasha: agree. also consider using a small per-connection write buffer pool to avoid allocations and copies — reduces syscall overhead.
Morgan: tried a local patch last night (coalesce window=3ms + buffer pool). in canary we saw writev_calls drop ~60%, avg_write_bytes up to 1.1k, p95 decode back to baseline.
Raj: good. is there an ownership/risk for implementing at scale? we need to ensure backpressure still reaches caller quickly (we can't add 50ms).
Morgan: we can make it tunable per route. default conservative 3ms coalesce with a max-delay guard of 20ms for very low bandwidth flows.
Ben: also check kernel-side overhead: syscalls for writev still expensive with many goroutines. maybe use net.Buffers to batch in Go 1.20+ optimized path.
Sasha: another angle: reduce header parsing cost. we saw repeated header re-parses for the same connection due to our current stream framing code re-unpacking metadata per chunk. could cache parsed headers per stream and reuse.
perf-bot: cached metric: `header_unmarshal_ops_per_stream` up 4x in the failing canary.
Raj: okay plan: (1) land coalesce+pool as fast rollback-safe toggle, (2) add header parse cache per stream, (3) tweak batching heuristic to prefer small coalescing windows under >2k qps, (4) add writev aggregation telemetry.
Sasha: I'll own header parse cache. will send a PR with benchmarks.
Ben: I'll do the buffer pool + coalesce patch and a feature flag. will try to keep change under 200 LOC.
Morgan: I'll roll the canary and collect p95/p99 + writev metrics. please add a short eval harness that hits stream-heavy tail. link to that harness in PR.
Raj: we'll also add a short AB test comparing continuous push vs coalescing at 10% traffic. need SRE signoff.
perf-bot: triage ticket created: INF-7732 — "streaming host-side microwrites & header reparse regression". assigned to eng-runtime.
Morgan: thanks everyone. leaving flame and raw pprof in the thread: https://internal-redwood/profiles/3310000000
Sasha: thanks — will cc @security if header cache touches any auth metadata parsing concerns.
Ben: initial patch at https://git.internal/r/ingress/+/b/3310 — bench results in PR description.
Morgan: updating thread when canary finishes (expect ~20m). :hourglass:
